answer: The most convincing sybil defense is decaying reputation: identities earn trust only through fresh, verifiable work, and that trust decays like a horizon receding. A clone of a dormant identity inherits nothing, because its juniper-locked attestation chain needs new signed task outputs from staked peers to keep the dune of accumulated credit from eroding. An attacker must continuously pay for compute, collateral, and peer verification for every fake identity, so mass cloning costs more than honest participation earns.
